title: German Startup Trains Its Robots Using Humans Filming Themselves
source_used: The Star (Malaysia), which carries the Bloomberg story (Bloomberg original is behind a bot check)
key_facts: Germany's Agile Robots is training its machines by filming humans doing tasks, to make up for a shortage of data holding back industrial automation, its CEO says.
Its Robot Academy has workers film themselves, capturing hand and finger movements; the data is combined with other training data and robots practise in simulation.
CEO Zhaopeng Chen spoke on 8 Oct 2026 at the Wave by Vento event in Turin, Italy.
Robots can need thousands of attempts to learn a job and may have to relearn it after small changes, Chen said.
Agile Robots, formed in Munich in 2018 by German Aerospace Center researchers, says it has deployed more than 20,000 systems.
It has raised $1.5 billion to date and is in talks to raise a further $800 million with SoftBank involved, Bloomberg reported in June.
Neura Robotics, another German humanoid maker, is developing a robot training facility with the Technical University of Munich.
quote_evidence: Germany’s Agile Robots is training its machines by filming humans performing tasks, in a bid to compensate for a shortfall of data that is holding back industrial automation, according to its chief executive officer.
Agile Robots, formed in Munich in 2018 by researchers from the German Aerospace Center, has deployed more than 20,000 systems, according to the company.
Robots can require thousands of attempts to master a job and may need to learn it again after even small changes, Chen said.
why_it_matters_hint: Robots lack the large training sets that language models had, so firms are paying for human footage.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked; read The Star's republication, which credits Bloomberg. Figures are the company's and its CEO's.
